cf.title: DISTINCT in plain aggregate window functions

input.subject: [PATCH] DISTINCT in plain aggregate window functions

verdict_reasoning: The goal has lasting demand, and no surviving objection questions it. Two design points would likely stop a committer before code review. The grow-only hash table ignores work_mem with no plan to bound it (maintenance-fit-1), and patch 1 lets create view store queries that no release can run (replication-ondisk-1). The frame-dependent type support and value order (standards-compat-2) and the undocumented partial subset (standards-compat-3) also need agreement on the list.

brief.title: Allow distinct in plain aggregate window functions, by frame shape
brief.problem: Postgres rejects queries such as count(DISTINCT x) OVER (PARTITION BY p) at parse time with "DISTINCT is not implemented for window functions". The thread does not name users who asked for this. The author also says the parse-time rejection blocks view round-tripping and any later executor work.
brief.proposed_design: An eight-patch roadmap adds support step by step, by frame class and then by feature. Posted patches 1-3 carry DISTINCT through parse and deparse with a new WindowFunc field. They run whole-partition frames once per partition through sort and dedup, and grow-only frames (UNBOUNDED PRECEDING, no EXCLUDE) through an incremental hash table of values already seen.
user_visible_surface: SQL: agg(DISTINCT x) OVER (...) is accepted for plain aggregates with a single argument and supported frame shapes.
Error moves from parse time to executor init: "DISTINCT is not yet implemented for window aggregates" (FEATURE_NOT_SUPPORTED) for frames still out of scope.
pg_get_viewdef() and stored rules now print DISTINCT on window aggregates.
Node change: new boolean windistinct field in WindowFunc, visible to extensions that read parse trees.
Grow-only frames reject argument types that are not hashable, such as money.
author_claims: Splitting the work by frame shape matters more than splitting by aggregate kind, because moving frames are the hard part.
Whole-partition results are constant per partition, so the executor finalizes once and reuses the result.
Mixed DISTINCT and non-DISTINCT window aggregates work in one query.
Different array_agg(DISTINCT ...) value order between the two paths is not a correctness issue, because the standard does not fix that order.
The unbounded memory of the grow-only hash path is a known limitation, not the intended end state.
brief.thread_state: Henson Choi reviewed v2 and found results matching equivalent rewrites, but raised hashability, value order, unbounded hash memory, coverage gaps and missing docs. The author posted v3 with more tests and documented limits, and kept the patch split; no one has replied to v3.
unclear: The patches do not bound the grow-only hash table by work_mem, and no plan to fix it is given.
No SGML documentation exists yet for the new syntax or its frame limits.
The roadmap does not say whether frames starting at CURRENT ROW will be supported, which is where RPR would meet this feature.
The material gives no performance numbers against GROUP BY or correlated subquery rewrites.
No one has said whether partial support that changes with frame shape is acceptable to commit before the sliding-frame patches.

prior_attempts.title: window function improvements WIP
prior_attempts.quote: I think that Vik Fearing's patch about "Implement <null treatment> for window functions" is much clear, better and has a chance to be committed.
prior_attempts.reason: Tom Lane asked whether DISTINCT on a window function is well defined, given one output row per input row and order sensitivity. He also objected to datatype-specific code, so the author suspended the DISTINCT work. Surafel Temesgen's review of the null treatment patch found white space errors, uncommented functions, oversized regression tests and an unexplained change to makeBoolAConst. The author then judged Vik Fearing's competing <null treatment> patch the better design and offered to withdraw his own, and Michael Paquier closed the entry.
prior_attempts.what_is_different: This series uses generic sort and hash support for the argument type, with no code tied to specific data types. [P4] moved on to a different feature after review.

objections.title: Grow-only hash path ignores work_mem with no plan to bound it
objections.failure_scenario: A user runs count(DISTINCT user_id) OVER (PARTITION BY tenant ORDER BY ts) on a large, high-cardinality partition. The hash table holds every distinct value, so the backend grows past work_mem without spilling. The operator finds out when the backend or the whole server hits out-of-memory.
objections.argument: Message #3 shows that every comparable path spills at work_mem, including HashAgg and the patch's own sort path, and this one does not. Message #4 and the v3-0003 commit message call it a known limitation that "would require additional design", but they give no design and no target patch. A committer who pushes patch 3 owns a memory-unbounded executor path in a released version.
objections.author_must_show: How will the grow-only path stay within work_mem, and will that land before or together with patch 3?

critic.reasoning: Message #4 and the v3-0003 commit message confirm that the hash table ignores work_mem, and they give no design or target patch. Naming the limitation in comments does not bound the memory.

objections.title: Stored views can hold DISTINCT window aggregates that never execute
objections.failure_scenario: A user runs create view with count(distinct x) over (partition by p order by o rows between 3 preceding and current row). The view is stored in pg_rewrite, dumped and restored without complaint. Every select on it then fails at executor init with FEATURE_NOT_SUPPORTED, and the user finds out only when the application queries the view.
objections.argument: Patch 1 moves the rejection from parse analysis to executor init for all frame shapes. The frame clause is fully known at parse analysis, so unsupported shapes could still be rejected there. Only the supported shapes need to reach stored rules. The author's reason, that parse-time rejection blocks view round-tripping, applies to supported shapes only, and for the others it lets the catalog keep rules that no release can run until patches 4-6 land.
objections.author_must_show: Why not keep the parse-time error for frame shapes the executor cannot run, so pg_rewrite never stores a view that fails on every execution?

critic.reasoning: The frame options are known at parse analysis, so unsupported shapes could still be rejected there. The commit message's round-trip reason covers only shapes the executor can run.

objections.title: Accepted types and value order depend on the frame shape
objections.failure_scenario: A report uses count(DISTINCT amount::money) OVER (PARTITION BY p) and works. A later edit adds ORDER BY o for a running total, and the same aggregate fails at execution because money is not hashable. array_agg(DISTINCT x) returns values in a different order after the same edit.
objections.argument: Message #3 shows that GROUP BY agg(DISTINCT x) accepts sortable but non-hashable types, while patch 3 rejects them on grow-only frames. Message #4 defers this as an executor-level decision, but it is part of the user contract once committed. Non-window DISTINCT feeds sorted input in practice, and users depend on that order even though the standard does not require it. A prior attempt drew a question on whether DISTINCT window aggregates are well defined under order sensitivity [P4].
objections.author_must_show: Can the grow-only path fall back to sort for non-hashable types, and what array_agg(DISTINCT) order will the documentation promise across frame shapes?

critic.reasoning: Message #4 concedes both differences and defers them, so the thread does not answer the objection. It stands on message #3 alone; [P4] records a question, so it should not be cited as support.

objections.title: Partial support by frame shape ships with no documented contract
objections.failure_scenario: A release ships patches 1-3 only. Users find by trial that OVER (PARTITION BY p) works and OVER (ROWS 3 PRECEDING) does not, with no SGML entry listing the supported frames. If the sliding-frame patches stall, that frame-dependent rule stays for years.
objections.argument: Message #4 confirms there are no SGML changes and that docs are deferred to the full series. Patches 4-8 have no code posted, and message #4 says CURRENT ROW-start frames have not been studied. The project would commit a syntax whose valid forms depend on frame class, with no plan to finish if the later work stops.
objections.author_must_show: Is the patches 1-3 subset a complete, documentable feature on its own if patches 4-8 never land?

critic.reasoning: Message #4 defers the SGML changes to the full series, and patches 4-8 have no posted code. The thread does not say whether patches 1-3 are a complete feature if the rest stalls.

refuted.title: Plan-dependent value order revives the earlier well-definedness concern
refuted.failure_scenario: A user writes array_agg(DISTINCT x) over (partition by p) and gets one element order. Adding order by o to the window changes the frame to grow-only, and the same values come back in a different order. They find out when a report or a test diff changes after an unrelated query edit.
refuted.argument: The summary of [P4] says an earlier DISTINCT-in-window attempt stalled partly on whether the construct is well defined for order-sensitive aggregates. Message #3 shows patches 2 and 3 order distinct values differently: sort in one path, hash in the other. Message #4 answers that the standard does not fix this order and that the difference should be documented, but no SGML exists yet. Plain array_agg(DISTINCT x) feeds values in sorted order, so a committer would likely ask why the window form departs from it.
refuted.author_must_show: Why should the grow-only path not feed distinct values in the same sorted order as plain aggregate DISTINCT, so the result does not depend on frame shape?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of standards-compat-2, which covers the same value-order difference together with the type restriction.

refuted.title: Rejection moves to executor init, so stored objects accept queries that cannot run
refuted.failure_scenario: A user creates a view or a BEGIN ATOMIC function with count(DISTINCT x) OVER (PARTITION BY p ORDER BY o ROWS 3 PRECEDING). The create succeeds, pg_dump and restore succeed, and the error appears only when someone queries the view in production. If patch 1 is committed alone, every DISTINCT window aggregate is in this state.
refuted.argument: Patch 1 removes the parse-time error and adds a FEATURE_NOT_SUPPORTED error at WindowAgg init. Postgres rejects unsupported syntax at parse analysis, so creating a view proves it can run. The frame clause and argument type are known at parse analysis, so the scope check could stay there. The commit message gives view round-tripping as the reason, but a view that cannot run has nothing useful to round-trip.
refuted.author_must_show: Why can the frame-shape and type scope check not run at parse analysis, so that unsupported forms still fail at create view time?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of replication-ondisk-1, which states the same executor-init concern and adds that only supported shapes need to reach stored rules.

refuted.title: Grow-only hash path lets any user exceed work_mem without limit
refuted.failure_scenario: A user with only SELECT privilege runs count(DISTINCT x) OVER (PARTITION BY p ORDER BY o) on a large, high-cardinality partition. The hash table in patch 3 keeps every distinct value and never spills, so the backend grows until the OOM killer or overcommit failure hits. Other sessions then lose their connections or the postmaster restarts.
refuted.argument: Message #3 shows that every comparable path is work_mem-bounded, including HashAgg, and that the patch's own whole-partition path is too. The v3 commit message and message #4 confirm the gap and give no plan to close it. Administrators set work_mem to bound per-node memory, and this new node path quietly ignores that bound. Aggregates such as array_agg can already grow transition state without limit, but that cost is visible in the aggregate's output, and this hash table is internal state.
refuted.author_must_show: Can patch 3 bound its hash table by work_mem, by spilling or by falling back to sort, before it is committed?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of maintenance-fit-1. The privilege framing adds little, because the objection itself notes that array_agg already lets any user grow memory without limit.

refuted.title: Unsupported frame shapes now fail at executor start
refuted.failure_scenario: A user creates a view with count(DISTINCT x) OVER (ORDER BY o ROWS 3 PRECEDING). CREATE VIEW succeeds and pg_dump restores it. Every SELECT and plain EXPLAIN then fails with FEATURE_NOT_SUPPORTED, so the user finds out only when someone queries the view.
refuted.argument: v3-0001 moves the rejection from parse analysis to WindowAgg initialization. That change lets stored rules hold queries that can never run. Frame shape, argument count and hashability of the argument type are all known at parse analysis or plan time. Postgres normally rejects unsupported constructs before it stores them. The commit message's reason, round-tripping views, needs only the representation, and it does not explain why the scope check must wait until executor start.
refuted.author_must_show: Why can the frame-shape, arity and hashability checks not run at parse analysis or planning, so CREATE VIEW rejects queries that cannot execute?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of replication-ondisk-1, which describes the same stored-view failure.

refuted.title: Partial series fixes executor strategy choice with no committer engaged
refuted.failure_scenario: Patches 1-3 are committed and the remaining five stall. The release ships DISTINCT window support that depends on frame shape, has two executor-chosen strategies with different type support and different array_agg value order, and has no SGML documentation. Later sliding-frame work must keep that behaviour or change it.
refuted.argument: Only one reviewer is visible, in message #3, and no committer has replied to v1, v2 or v3. In message #4 the author kept the executor-level hash-or-sort choice and deferred planner-driven selection, RANGE and GROUPS coverage, and documentation. Message #3 notes that the grow-only path is a special case of patches 4-6. So patch 3 may add a second path that the later refcounted design makes redundant.
refuted.author_must_show: Which committed subset of the roadmap would be a complete, documented feature on its own if the later patches never land?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of standards-compat-3 on the stalled-series risk, and message #4 answers the redundancy point for patch 3. The lack of a committer belongs in the committability field.

refuted.title: Patches 2-3 cover frames that existing rewrites already handle
refuted.failure_scenario: A user who needs count(DISTINCT x) per partition today joins a GROUP BY subquery back on p, or uses a correlated subquery. After this series they can write it inline, but only for whole-partition and UNBOUNDED PRECEDING frames. The sliding frames that have no simple rewrite stay rejected until patches 4-6.
refuted.argument: In message #3 the reviewer checked the new results against correlated subquery and GROUP BY rewrites and found them equal, so these frame shapes are reachable today. Running counts also have a known idiom: sum the rows where row_number() over (partition by p, x order by o) = 1. The thread argues for parse and view round-tripping but does not say what users cannot do now. A committer would likely ask whether shorter syntax for two frame classes justifies a permanent executor path with an unbounded hash table.
refuted.author_must_show: Which users need these frame shapes inline, and what do the GROUP BY or correlated subquery rewrites fail to do for them beyond being longer to write?

critic.reasoning: The material shows demand that lasted: [P1], [P2] and [P4] are earlier attempts by two other authors, and message #3 says Oracle runs the whole-partition forms. [P2] records that no one objected to the design.

touch_points.label: catalog changes
touch_points.reason: The new windistinct field in WindowFunc changes stored rules in pg_rewrite and needs a catversion bump.

touch_points.label: ABI / extension API
touch_points.reason: Extensions that read or build WindowFunc nodes see the new windistinct field in primnodes.h.

touch_points.label: SQL-standard conflict or non-standard syntax
touch_points.reason: The series accepts agg(DISTINCT x) OVER (...), but only for some frame shapes and argument types.

touch_points.label: planner behaviour change
touch_points.reason: Patch 1 touches clauses.c, and the executor chooses sort or hash where message #3 suggests the planner should.

touch_points.label: pg_dump / restore round-trip
touch_points.reason: ruleutils.c now prints DISTINCT on window aggregates, so views with unsupported frames dump and restore but fail when queried.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: see objection standards-compat-3: Partial support by frame shape ships with no documented contract

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: Patches 2 and 3 add two DISTINCT paths to nodeWindowAgg.c, and five roadmap patches have no posted code.

touch_points.label: performance on the hot path
touch_points.reason: The grow-only hash table is not bounded by work_mem, and the series changes the WindowAgg aggregate code.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: How will the grow-only hash table stay within work_mem, and will that land before or together with patch 3?
Why not keep the parse-time error for frame shapes the executor cannot run, so that create view rejects them?
Can the grow-only path fall back to sort for types that are sortable but not hashable, such as money?
What order of values will the documentation promise for array_agg(DISTINCT x) across whole-partition and grow-only frames?
Are patches 1-3 a complete feature that can be documented on its own if patches 4-8 never land?

committability.owner_note: It needs a committer who knows window frame execution in nodeWindowAgg.c and the parse and ruleutils handling of WindowFunc. No committer has spoken in the visible thread.
committability.liability: The owner signs for SQL syntax whose valid forms depend on frame shape, a new field in stored rules, and a hash path with no memory bound. This lasts until the later roadmap patches land.
committability.author_follow_up: The author posted v2 and v3, answered the review of v2, and moved the entry to the next CommitFest in September 2026.

priority.reason: Three earlier attempts in [P1], [P2] and [P4] and Oracle support noted in message #3 show lasting demand. Three patches of about 60 KiB, mostly in nodeWindowAgg.c, need a memory bound and a decision on where unsupported frames fail before detailed review.

provisional_note: Without the code, the per-row cost for window aggregates that do not use DISTINCT could not be checked. Both paths are also unchecked for strict aggregates and pass-by-reference types.

precedents_retrieved.title: parallel distinct union and aggregate support patch
precedents_retrieved.objectors: David Steele, David Rowley, Daniel Gustafsson
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a Parallel BatchSort node, and later a batch HashAggregate, that hash-partitions tuples into shared batches so each parallel worker sorts or aggregates whole batches for distinct, union and aggregate. A later version replaced this with an unbuffered Parallel Redistribute node that sends tuples to workers through shared memory queues, spilling to a SharedTuplestore.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The entry was returned with feedback because the patch needed a rebase for many months and the thread stalled. It got no review for two commitfests, and David Steele and David Rowley said the author had not answered reviewers who suggested an unbuffered Parallel Partition style operator. The author posted a Redistribute version in September 2021, but the visible messages show no review of it.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Many months on and this patch still needs a rebase to apply, and the thread has
stalled.  I'm marking this Returned with Feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: window function improvements WIP
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch first allowed DISTINCT inside aggregates used as window functions, such as array_agg(DISTINCT week) over a frame, with code limited to int, float and numeric. After review the author stopped that work and posted a different patch that adds RESPECT/IGNORE NULLS to lag(), lead(), first_value(), last_value() and nth_value(), with negative positions in nth_value() to read the frame in reverse.

He also objected to datatype-specific code, so the author suspended the DISTINCT work. Surafel Temesgen's review of the null treatment patch found white space errors, uncommented functions, oversized regression tests and an unexplained change to makeBoolAConst. The author then judged Vik Fearing's competing <null treatment> patch the better design and offered to withdraw his own, and Michael Paquier closed the entry.

precedents_retrieved.title: Removing useless DISTINCT clauses
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch applies the existing GROUP BY optimization to plain DISTINCT. When a table's primary key columns are all in the DISTINCT clause, the planner drops the other columns of that table from the distinctClause.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane found that removing distinctClause items breaks the parser-enforced match between DISTINCT and ORDER BY, which create_distinct_paths relies on. With a primary key on (a,b), `select distinct * from t1 order by a,c,b` hits an assertion and crashes the server. He judged the fix too large for the last day of the commitfest.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Once I noticed that, I became convinced that this patch actually
breaks planning of sort/unique-based DISTINCT: if we have a pkey a,b,
but the ORDER BY list is a,c,b, then we will sort by a,c,b but the
Unique node will be told it only needs to unique-ify on the first two
sort columns.

precedents_retrieved.title: Remove useless distinct clauses
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes the planner drop a DISTINCT clause when the selected columns include the primary key of a table, and turns inner joins to other tables into semi-joins. When the query has no ORDER BY, it uses the DISTINCT columns as the sort clause.
precedents_retrieved.objection: David Rowley found that the patch returns wrong results: with cross joins, select distinct a from t cross join pg_class cross join pg_attribute returns many rows where it should return one, because the change from inner joins to semi-joins is broken. He also objected that the patch clears parse->distinctClause directly, has no comments on why each transformation is valid, and does not follow the source format. The author did not answer the review, so Michael Paquier marked the entry Returned with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Also, the processing of the join tree where you switch inner joins to
semi joins looks broken.  This would require much more careful and
recursive processing to do properly.

precedents_retrieved.title: Implement <null treatment> for window functions
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds the SQL-standard RESPECT NULLS and IGNORE NULLS syntax to all true window functions, without hardcoding the standard's list of functions, and adds TREAT NULLS to CREATE FUNCTION. It does not implement FROM LAST.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The patch failed to compile under GCC with -Werror because 'step' may be used uninitialized in WinGetFuncArgInPartition and WinGetFuncArgInFrame. No new version came in for two months, so Michael Paquier marked it returned with feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: possibility to write window function in PL languages (like PLpgSQL)
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lets users write window functions in PL/pgSQL, using a special windowobject variable and SQL-callable wrappers around the C WindowObject API. Values fetched from the window arguments come back through a new proxy type, typedvalue, which PL/pgSQL assignment casts to the target variable's type.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane rejected the typedvalue type: its hard-wired set of conversions would have to grow to cover every built-in cast and could not handle extension types. He proposed dedicated PL/pgSQL syntax instead, and said access to partition local memory should stay out of a first version. The author withdrew the entry, saying a direct mapping of the WindowObject API looks like Cobol and that the declarative syntax needs a different concept.

precedents_retrieved.title: [WIP] Show a human-readable n_distinct in pg_stats view
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch changes the pg_stats view to show n_distinct as an absolute count of distinct values, computed from the negative fraction that pg_statistic.stadistinct stores when distinct values exceed 10% of rows. The author also asked whether to add a column showing that the estimate scales with table size.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Laurenz Albe objected that the change would help users confused by negative values but obscure the meaning for users who understand it, and that the pg_stats documentation already explains the semantics. No other reviewer replied, and the author later withdrew the entry without answering the objection.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
This may make things easier for those who are confused by a negative
entry, but it will obfuscate matters for those who are not.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert "Optimize order of GROUP BY keys".
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert "Optimize order of GROUP BY keys".
Reverted commit(s): Optimize order of GROUP BY keys
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit db0d67db2401eb6238ccc04c6407a4fd4f985832 and
several follow-on fixes.  The idea of making a cost-based choice
of the order of the sorting columns is not fundamentally unsound,
but it requires cost information and data statistics that we don't
really have.  For example, relying on procost to distinguish the
relative costs of different sort comparators is pretty pointless
so long as most such comparator functions are labeled with cost 1.0.
Moreover, estimating the number of comparisons done by Quicksort
requires more than just an estimate of the number of distinct values
in the input: you also need some idea of the sizes of the larger
groups, if you want an estimate that's good to better than a factor of
three or so.  That's data that's often unknown or not very reliable.
Worse, to arrive at estimates of the number of calls made to the
lower-order-column comparison functions, the code needs to make
estimates of the numbers of distinct values of multiple columns,
which are necessarily even less trustworthy than per-column stats.
Even if all the inputs are perfectly reliable, the cost algorithm
as-implemented cannot offer useful information about how to order
sorting columns beyond the point at which the average group size
is estimated to drop to 1.

Close inspection of the code added by db0d67db2 shows that there
are also multiple small bugs.  These could have been fixed, but
there's not much point if we don't trust the estimates to be
accurate in-principle.

Finally, the changes in cost_sort's behavior made for very large
changes (often a factor of 2 or so) in the cost estimates for all
sorting operations, not only those for multi-column GROUP BY.
That naturally changes plan choices in many situations, and there's
precious little evidence to show that the changes are for the better.
Given the above doubts about whether the new estimates are really
trustworthy, it's hard to summon much confidence that these changes
are better on the average.

Since we're hard up against the release deadline for v15, let's
revert these changes for now.  We can always try again later.

Note: in v15, I left T_PathKeyInfo in place in nodes.h even though
it's unreferenced.  Removing it would be an ABI break, and it seems
a bit late in the release cycle for that.

roaster_notes.note: The earlier attempts ended over process problems or for reasons not recorded. Only the order-sensitivity point from [P4] may still apply, and it is raised above.
Three objections raised. Value order and hashability are combined into one.

The only persistent change is the new windistinct field in WindowFunc, stored in pg_rewrite and needing a catversion bump. There is no WAL, on-disk relation format, wire protocol or replication change.
The proposal adds no new privilege, role or object type. Aggregates run with the caller's rights as they do today, so the only security issue is the unbounded memory use described above.
Objections were found from the maintenance and fit angle. Per-tuple cost for non-DISTINCT window queries could not be checked without the code.
No extension or contrib module provides DISTINCT window aggregates, so only the query-rewrite alternative applies from this angle.

The thread names no users, but [P1], [P2] and [P4] show three earlier attempts by two authors between 2020 and 2024, and message #3 confirms Oracle supports the whole-partition forms. The cost falls mostly on queries that use DISTINCT, and a committer would likely accept the long-standing parse-time error as evidence of a real gap.
